title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is a 1986 first draft of an axiomatic, combinatorial 'analysis situs', in the spirit of the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse. The objects are 'figures' with three relations:
- ≤ : subfigure.
- ⪯ : a second, stronger inclusion relation, read here as 'closed subfigure'.
- ≪ : a relation defined on p.77 by K ≪ G iff K ≤ Ḡ ⪯ G for some Ḡ. It is a kind of 'relatively compact / way-below' inclusion.
There is also a distinguished class M of finite figures, the 'multiplicités'. They behave like cells or simplices, each with a boundary ∂Y equal to the union of its proper sub-multiplicités. A strengthened relation ⋘ appears as well.

Lemma 2 (continuing Lemma 1 of p.77). Take G ≤ F, F' a sub-object of F, and G' = G ∩ F'. If K ≪ G and K ≪ F', then K ≪ G'. So G ∩ F' is an infimum for ≪. Lemma 1 handled the case G ⪯ F. The intended proof is the same: write K ≤ Ḡ ⪯ G and invoke axiom C6. Grothendieck starts this ('On a ici encore K ≤ Ḡ ⪇ G, et ...') and then writes 'J'abandonne ! ...', referring back to the text at page 51.

Marginal NB. The pullback map F' ↦ G' = G ∩ F', from subfigures of F to subfigures of G, commutes with arbitrary Sups and with arbitrary ≤-Infs. In other words, restriction to G is a complete lattice homomorphism, as for opens or sieves under pullback.

An aborted 'C8' is crossed out. It is then restated as a Proposition. Let F be a figure and X ∈ M with X ≪ F.
- (a) There exists Y ∈ M, Y ≤ F, with X ⋘ Y.
- (b) Among such Y there is a smallest one. It is characterised by the condition that the subfigure of X induced by ∂Y is ≠ X.

This is the axiomatic version of the 'carrier' of a cell in a CW or simplicial complex. A singular cell lands in a unique smallest closed cell, namely the one whose boundary does not contain it.

Proof of (a). F = Sup of its sub-multiplicités Y_i. By C6(c), pulling back along X gives X = Sup_i G_i, where G_i is the subfigure of X induced by Y_i. A multiplicité is 'irreducible' (join-prime / supercompact) for this Sup. Hence X = G_i for some i, i.e. X ≪ Y_i.

Part (b) is proved on p.79. One picks a minimal Y using finite combinatorial dimension. Uniqueness then follows from F_Y ∩ F_{Y'} = F_{Y∩Y'}, i.e. stability of induced subfigures under intersection, together with minimality.
errors: Lemma 2 is left unproved: Grothendieck explicitly abandons it ('J'abandonne !') and refers back to p.51 instead of completing the argument.

In the proof of (a), the step 'X = Sup_i G_i ⇒ ∃ i, X = G_i' silently uses that a multiplicité is join-prime / compact for arbitrary Sups. That property is not stated on this page. If the family Y_i is infinite, it needs a compactness axiom.
The relation ⋘ in (a) is used without definition on this page. On p.79 it is used as X ≪ Y meaning F_Y = X, so the notation is somewhat inconsistent.

ideas.what: Intersection G∩F' is the infimum for the 'way-below' relation ≪ on subfigures (Lemmas 1–2)
ideas.modern_name: meet-stability of a way-below / relatively-compact relation; finite intersections of compact-closure inclusions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in continuous lattice theory (Scott, Gierz et al., 1970s)

ideas.what: Pullback F'↦G∩F' from subfigures of F to subfigures of G preserves arbitrary sups and infs
ideas.modern_name: pullback of subobjects as a complete lattice homomorphism (frame/coframe morphism; Heyting-category property)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Topos theory / locale theory (Lawvere, Tierney, Joyal 1970s)

ideas.what: Every finite cell X lying 'compactly' in a figure F lands in a unique smallest cell Y of F, characterised by X not factoring through ∂Y
ideas.modern_name: carrier (support) of a cell/simplex in a CW or simplicial complex; unique minimal face; Eilenberg–Zilber-type unique non-degenerate factorisation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (J.H.C. Whitehead CW complexes; Eilenberg–Zilber lemma 1950)

ideas.what: Multiplicités as join-irreducible (supercompact) generators of the lattice of subfigures
ideas.modern_name: completely join-prime elements / supercompact objects generating a presheaf-like category

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly abandons the proof of Lemma 2 (meet-stability of ≪ when G ≤ F) rather than completing it. This is part of the unpublished axiomatic 'analysis situs' (figures/multiplicités) that was never developed into a published theory of tame/combinatorial topology.
missed.quote: J'abandonne ! Il serait ennuyeux de reprendre au texte page 51.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor as a single lemma. It does document that the 1986 axiomatic tame-topology programme stalled on technical lattice-theoretic verifications. That is relevant to the history of 'topologie modérée'. It could be compared with o-minimal and stratified-space axiomatics, or with Lurie/Ayala–Francis–Tanaka stratified frameworks.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a routine but genuine axiomatisation step: the carrier of a cell, and meet/sup-stability of induced subfigures. It sits inside an unpublished 1986 attempt at an axiomatic analysis situs. The explicit 'J'abandonne' is a nice historical detail, but the mathematics itself is classical.
transcription_corrections: 'On a [?] encore K ≤ Ḡ ⪇ G' reads 'On a ici encore K ≤ Ḡ ⪇ G, et ...'.
Lemma 2 diagram: the vertical relations are ∨∨ (≫-type), as on p.77, and G' = G∩F' is written below G'.
'∃ Y é[?], ... de F' in the crossed C8 is probably '∃ Y ∈ M, ... de F'.
In b), '[?] somme [?] figure de X induite par ∂Y' should read 'la sous-figure de X induite par ∂Y'.
The first line of the crossed C8 ends with 'X une multi-' (multiplicité), consistent with the later 'X ∈ M'.
Marginal NB: 'commute aux Sup quelconques et aux Inf_≤ quelconques'.
